Use this notebook to confirm that the R environment is available, that `reticulate` can see the conda environment, and that basic plotting works in R.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE)
# Declare the notebook location so here() can resolve project-relative paths.
here::i_am("notebooks/00_r_first_test_notebook.Rmd")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir=here::here())

# Load the shared project setup used across scripts and notebooks.
source(here::here("setup", "R", "setup_reticulate.R"))
library(ggplot2)

# Bind reticulate to the project conda environment before importing Python.
setup_reticulate()
```

```{r}
# Show which Python interpreter reticulate resolved for this R session.
reticulate::py_config()
```

```{r}
# Import the Python helper and call it from R.
reticulate::source_python(here::here("python", "helpers.py"))
values <- c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)
summarize_values(values)
```

## Read a small dummy dataset

```{r}
# Load a small CSV from the data folder for simple plotting examples.
sales_data <- read.csv(here::here("data", "raw", "dummy_sales.csv"))
sales_data$month <- factor(sales_data$month, levels=unique(sales_data$month))
sales_data
```

## Plot monthly sales by region

```{r}
# Plot the monthly sales trend for each region.
ggplot(sales_data, aes(x=month, y=sales, color=region, group=region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth=1) +
  geom_point(size=2) +
  labs(title="Monthly Sales by Region", x="Month", y="Sales") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Compare total orders by category

```{r}
# Aggregate orders by category and plot them as a simple bar chart.
category_orders <- aggregate(orders ~ category, data=sales_data, sum)

ggplot(category_orders, aes(x=category, y=orders, fill=category)) +
  geom_col(width=0.7) +
  labs(title="Total Orders by Category", x="Category", y="Orders") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position="none")
```
